t: Carlube engine oil | BobIsTheOilGuy
s: February 1, 2025 - If you can find something like this in the Netherlands for a decent price with approvals not "recommendations" or "meets and/or exceeds" or "performance profile" I would buy it. https://www.opieoils.co.uk/p-197007-valvoline-synpower-5w-40-fully-synthetic-engine-oil.aspx ... Toyota's that spec 0w-16 as the minimum can use 15w40 as the max and Toyota engines that spec 0w-20 can use 20w-50 as the max. If you're not doing extended intervals you could use a synthetic blend and be ok but the price difference is rarely large enough to make it worth while. I would only ever see myself using mannol, millers, this carlube stuff, or something similar if it is at least a 40 grade incase the oil is slightly underadditzed as thicker oil helps with wear but I still wouldn't buy it when there are better options for a bit more.
